Committee: Boards, Agencies and Commissions
Sponsor: Wood (R)
Analyst: Robin Rawls
Date: 02/23/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 10 as introduced codifies the current practice of the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners by authorizing the board to charge and collect certain fees by rule. This bill would allow the board to continue charging a license verification fee of $12.50 each, and a fee to act as a continuing education provider at $75 per module, while also allowing the board to establish fees for other services. The board collects approximately $50,000 annually for these two fees.
Howard Sanderford, Chair
Boards, Agencies and Commissions

Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Security
Sponsor: Sorrell
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 03/08/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 368 as introduced creates a violation for transporting a dog or cat on a flatbed truck without securing them in a cage and provides for a fine up to $50 for the first offense and a fine up to $200 for subsequent offenses.  This could increase receipts to the State General Fund, by an undetermined amount, dependent upon the number of violations issued and fines collected.
Allen Farley, Vice Chair
Public Safety and Homeland Security

Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
Sponsor: Gaston
Analyst: Robin Rawls
Date: 02/25/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 68 as passed the House of Representatives provides for the continuance of the Board of Hearing Instrument Dealers until October 1, 2025 pursuant to the Alabama Sunset Law. This bill will not otherwise affect state or local funding.
Steve Livingston, Chairperson
Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
